name: Egypt
known: The pyramids of Giza and ancient Egypt
The River Nile
The Suez Canal, a shortcut between Europe and Asia
Tourism and cotton
facts: Most of the country is desert, so nearly everyone lives along the Nile and its delta.
The Suez Canal links the Mediterranean and the Red Sea and carries a large share of the world's shipping.
Cairo is one of the largest cities in Africa and the Arab world.

name: Ethiopia
known: Being the birthplace of coffee
Long-distance running champions
Lalibela's churches carved out of rock
Ethiopian Airlines, Africa's largest airline
facts: It was never colonised, apart from a short Italian occupation from 1936 to 1941.
Addis Ababa is the home of the African Union.
Ethiopia uses its own calendar, with 13 months, about seven to eight years behind the Gregorian one.
It is one of the most populous countries in Africa and has no coastline.

name: Ghana
known: Gold and cocoa
Being the first country in sub-Saharan Africa to win independence from colonial rule, in 1957
Kente cloth and highlife music
Football and the national team, the Black Stars
facts: The capital is Accra, on the Atlantic coast.
Lake Volta, created by the Akosombo Dam, is one of the largest man-made lakes in the world by surface area.
English is the official language, but most people also speak a local language such as Akan.

name: Kenya
known: Safaris in the Maasai Mara and the wildebeest migration
World-class long-distance runners
Tea, coffee and cut flowers
M-Pesa, a pioneer of mobile money
facts: Nairobi is a regional tech and business hub, nicknamed the Silicon Savannah.
Mount Kenya, the country's namesake, is the second-highest mountain in Africa.
It became independent from Britain in 1963.

name: Morocco
known: The old cities of Marrakech and Fes
Phosphates, of which it holds the world's largest reserves
Car and aircraft-parts factories serving Europe
Football: a World Cup semi-finalist in 2022 and a co-host of the 2030 tournament
facts: The capital is Rabat; the largest city and main business centre is Casablanca.
The country has coasts on both the Atlantic and the Mediterranean, the Atlas Mountains and part of the Sahara.
The University of al-Qarawiyyin in Fes, founded in 859, is often described as one of the oldest universities still operating.

name: Nigeria
known: Nollywood, one of the world's biggest film industries by number of films
Afrobeats music
Oil exports
A fast-growing technology and fintech scene in Lagos
facts: It is the most populous country in Africa.
Lagos is the biggest city; the capital has been Abuja since 1991.
It became independent from Britain in 1960, and more than 250 ethnic groups live there.

name: South Africa
known: Safaris and wildlife, such as Kruger National Park
Gold, platinum and diamond mining
Table Mountain and Cape Town
Nelson Mandela and the end of apartheid
facts: It has three capitals: Pretoria (government), Cape Town (parliament) and Bloemfontein (courts).
Eleven spoken languages are official, and South African Sign Language became the twelfth in 2023.
The first fully democratic election was held in 1994.
